title: 一本の花を描く (HANA Gesture Study)

revisits.note: Remote Compute v0 Milestone 1 adds the pure katachi.hana-finalization-snapshot.v0 boundary and shared hana-cpu-js-v0 Finalization Core. It reuses the existing Smooth Centerline, dense Material Samples, KD-tree Point Field, cooperative Z-slice meshing, and validation path, returning typed-array Mesh data without DOM, Three.js, Pointer Event, or Authoring Document persistence. Milestone 2 adds the Local / Windows / Auto backend interface with AbortSignal, health/work estimation, identity checks, strict Remote diagnostics, and Local fallback. Auto initially selects Windows for 512+ Material Samples or 200,000+ estimated voxels; iPad Remote Gate and the Windows service remain pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 3 adds a Windows Node CPU service on loopback with bounded worker_threads, bounded request / queue / output limits, health and capability endpoints, finalize / cancel endpoints, worker crash replacement, and the versioned katachi.hana-compute-wire.v0 binary typed-array Mesh response. The service reuses the same hana-cpu-js-v0 core, stores no Authoring Document, exposes gpu=false, and provides no file or code execution surface. Software server, binary protocol, cancellation boundary, malformed-request, and existing HANA checks pass; iPad Remote Gate remains pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 1 adds katachi.hana-document.v2 migration, immutable Raw / provenance-preserving multi-Stroke authoring state, active and selected Stroke roles, revision-aware updates, world-space arc-length Soft Edit (LOW 0.75 / MEDIUM 1.50), and authoring-only Undo / Redo. Derived Material / Field / Surface / Proxy data remains outside the saved document. Software checks pass; hardware recheck for multi-Stroke UI remains pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 2 adds deterministic arc-length Gesture Channels for pressure and speed, zero/tiny-delta and outlier handling, Uniform / Pressure / Speed / Pressure+Speed Material Mapping, configurable radius bounds and influences, provenance-preserving derived profiles, and a bounded live profile path. Mapping settings are authoring state; derived radius samples remain unsaved. Software checks pass; hardware recheck remains pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 3 adds local Material Objects with bounds, sample cache, local candidate query, source revision and latest-only generation identity. Dirty invalidation is object-scoped, old generations are rejected, and the registry replaces rather than accumulates derived caches. Existing HANA-2A cooperative generation and sphere field baseline remain unchanged. Software checks pass; multi-object hardware recheck remains pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 4 adds deterministic gesture-authored Flower authoring from selected petal/core Strokes, local frame and provenance, immutable move / rotate / stem attachment, core Stroke addition, and Flower-scoped Material Object materialization. No random variation, global union, Mesh authority, or SKIN production change was introduced. Software checks pass; multi-Stroke Flower hardware recheck remains pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 5 adds an immutable semantic Authoring Graph with typed nodes, typed edges, junctions, cycles, connect / disconnect, graph overlay segments, source provenance, revision and protected flags. Validation detects missing endpoints, duplicate identifiers or connections, zero-length edges, and stale source object references. The graph remains HANA-local; no SKIN production behavior or Mesh authority was changed. Software checks pass; multi-Stroke Graph hardware recheck remains pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 6 adds the versioned katachi.hana-skin-bridge.v0 semantic export and validator. It carries Raw Gesture and adaptive Control Stroke identity, pressure / time / order / provenance, roles, material mapping intents, Flower and Graph semantics, units, source revision, and protected authoring boundaries. Derived Material Samples, Field, and Surface Mesh are excluded. SKIN production files and behavior remain unchanged; a future SKIN adapter is intentionally pending. Software checks pass; SKIN integration and hardware recheck remain pending.

Authoring stack v0 Milestone 7 adds a deterministic hana-authoring-study-v0 fixture with one Stem, one Core, five Petals, variable pressure-derived material profile, provenance, Flower attachment, junction / Graph, local Material Objects, Document JSON save / reload, authoring Undo / Redo, and semantic Bridge export / validation. The normal HANA URL exposes an additive HANA-local Load Study / Save Study / Load JSON / Export Bridge / Undo / Redo panel that regenerates from authoring Document data rather than loading demo Mesh. Existing four-view HANA and SKIN production behavior remain unchanged. Software checks pass; multi-Stroke hardware recheck remains pending.

Additional A adds a deterministic three-Flower small-cluster container built from the End-to-End authoring fixture. It preserves shared Stroke provenance while placing three Flower instances, builds branch / junction Graph edges, selects Flower-scoped local Material Objects, regenerates object-local caches, validates references, and serializes only Document / Flower / Graph / selection semantics. Derived Material Objects and Surface are excluded from cluster JSON; no global union or SKIN production change was introduced. Software checks pass; multi-Flower hardware recheck remains pending.

Additional B adds the HANA-local katachi.hana-surface-draw.v0 foundation contract without projection UI. Surface Draw anchors retain source Surface ID, ray hit position, local normal and tangent frame, source triangle, barycentric position, Raw Gesture provenance, and order. The contract is immutable and serializable; no Surface Mesh authority, raycast implementation, or SKIN production change was introduced. Software checks pass; Surface Draw hardware and projection recheck remain pending.

Additional C adds the HANA-local katachi.hana-silhouette-section.v0 representation and serialization contract. Silhouette plane, projected view direction, 2D contour, Section plane, Section curve, source Surface / Gesture provenance, and point order are retained with finite, provenance-length, and duplicate-ID validation. No contour extraction, projection UI, Surface authority, or SKIN production change was introduced. Software checks pass; projection and Section hardware recheck remain pending.

Additional D adds the isolated HANA-local katachi.hana-chunked-field-prototype.v0 Study contract. Fixed-size chunks, object-to-chunk reverse indexing, bounds-crossing membership, dirty-chunk-only deterministic cache regeneration, boundary coverage validation, and JSON serialization are implemented. The prototype is not connected to the normal Point Field / SDF or Surface path; dense Material Samples, Shape Fidelity, HANA-2A contracts, and SKIN production behavior remain unchanged. Software checks pass; hardware validation and any production Field integration remain pending separate design work.

HANA-1A starts an independent Four View Input Shell. It preserves viewport-local PointerEvent strokes, raw pressure, time, pointer identity and stroke order separately from camera/layout state. It deliberately does not create 3D Stroke, Graph, Field, Stem or Mesh data.

EasyCanvas and Apple Pencil verification passed with three pen strokes across Front / Right / Front, 988 ordered points, continuous non-binary pressure, monotonic time, JSON export and zero browser console warnings or errors. Front and Right remain separate 2D gestures by the HANA-1A Stop Gate; cross-view 3D linkage is deferred to HANA-1B.

HANA-1B introduces one shared editable Stroke3D derived from one immutable viewport Raw Gesture. It uses 32 deterministic arc-length controls with sourceT, raw interval, pressure and time provenance; orthographic edits change only the two visible axes and update all four projections. Stem, Field, Mesh and multi-stroke work remain excluded.

HANA-1B passed its EasyCanvas and Apple Pencil hardware gate with one Front pen Gesture containing 615 points, 241 continuous pressure values, one shared 32-control Stroke3D, four-view projection, Right-side depth edits, complete raw/provenance retention, separated JSON document state and zero browser console warnings or errors. The study stops before Stem or Field generation.

HANA-1C adds a regenerable open centripetal Catmull-Rom centerline with alpha 0.5 and eight samples per control segment, plus OFF / LOW / MEDIUM index-weighted Soft Edit. Raw Gesture and control provenance remain immutable; pressure is diagnostic data rather than line width or radius. Hardware verification remains required before PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-1C adds non-destructive 0.00–1.00 Smoothness through fixed four-pass relaxed display positions while keeping Raw Gesture, Control Stroke, provenance, pressure/time, 32 controls, Catmull-Rom settings, and 249 samples intact. EasyCanvas + Apple Pencil verification passed across the continuous 0.00–1.00 range, including 1.00; no optimum value is fixed, and the author selects Smoothness for the intended expression. Pencil is reserved primarily for Draw; precise control-point editing is mouse-oriented. Browser console warnings/errors were zero. HANA-1C is PASS / FROZEN; Stem / Field remain unstarted.

HANA-2A implementation stage initially added a regenerable 64-point arc-length Material Sample layer, equal-radius sphere Point Field with fixed blendK = radius * 0.5, and a CPU Preview Surface using the existing buildMeshFromField core at requested resolution 48. The later Long Stroke Scale Robustness refinement supersedes the fixed sample count with Thickness-driven spacing. Samples, Surface, Thickness, and Rebuild Surface are study-only preview controls; Material Samples, Field grid, and Preview Mesh are not added to the HANA document schema. Hardware verification remains required before HANA-2A PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Long Stroke Scale Robustness replaces fixed 64-point Material Samples with ceil(centerline arc length / radius) + 1 endpoint-preserving adaptive samples. Material Proxy and Surface use the same spacing-driven layer; long drawing prioritizes the requestAnimationFrame Proxy and may skip provisional SDF above the preview sample threshold. Requested Surface resolution remains 48, with only a minimal effective grid-resolution floor when thin long bounds would otherwise miss negative grid nodes. Adaptive Control Stroke density remains a follow-up; hardware verification remains required before PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A refinement keeps Surface visible during Mouse Right Edit: projected Surface/Centerline proximity selects the nearest Control Point parameter, existing Soft Edit updates the Control Stroke, and derived Centerline/Samples mark the previous Surface stale. Preview rebuilding is throttled to approximately 100ms during drag and finalized on mouseup. Apple Pencil remains Draw-only; hardware verification is still required before PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Live Surface Drawing refinement adds a non-persistent provisional Stroke3D / Smooth Centerline / Material Sample / Surface path during Apple Pencil Draw. Surface preview uses resolution 24 with approximately 100ms throttle, while pointerup regenerates the authoritative 32-control data and resolution 48 Surface immediately. Surface OFF skips Surface calculation; Rebuild Surface remains a manual/debug fallback. Smoothness algorithm is unchanged, and the EasyCanvas hardware gate remains pending before PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Smooth Live Material Preview adds a presentation-only Instanced Sphere Chain Material Proxy updated on requestAnimationFrame during Pencil Draw. The proxy follows provisional Material Samples at the current Thickness while the resolution 24 provisional SDF remains approximately 100ms-throttled. Pointerup removes the proxy and keeps the existing authoritative resolution 48 SDF pipeline. Provisional SDF min / median / max build durations are recorded for main-thread follow-up; Worker, WebGPU, CUDA, final Field, Smoothness, and pressure-radius changes remain out of scope. Hardware verification remains required before PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Long Stroke Live Proxy Performance separates Final adaptive Material Samples from live presentation. The live path is derived directly from Smooth Centerline and bounded to 192 Instanced Cylinder Segments, while dense adaptive Samples remain authoritative for final SDF Surface. Prefix replay of the 6956-point / 32.3-second fixture measured provisional Stroke, Smooth Centerline, adaptive Samples, and prior sphere-transform stages independently; the long presentation draw cost remains a hardware follow-up. HANA UI is touch-first for iPad Pro 11-inch with 48px+ hit areas, readable Smoothness / Thickness / Surface values, larger sliders, and Surface ON by default. Hardware verification remains required before PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Raw Gesture fidelity diagnosis found the main shape loss in the former 32-control Raw → Control resample: on the 2296-point fixture, Raw → Control was median / p95 / max 0.2925 / 0.8746 / 1.3288 with 68.3% beyond radius 0.18, while downstream Material Samples stayed close to Smooth Centerline. Authoritative pointerup fitting now selects ordered Raw samples by geometry error at a fixed editing fidelity budget of 0.09, independent of material Thickness, and refines against the derived Smooth Centerline; the 2296-point fixture produces 139 controls and the 6956-point / 32.3-second fixture produces 318 controls, with all measured Raw → Control / Smooth / Material errors below radius 0.18. Raw, pressure, time, order, provenance, Mouse Edit / Soft Edit, derived Material / Field / Surface layers, and the 192-segment Live Proxy cap remain intact. Provisional drawing keeps its bounded lightweight path for input performance. HANA-2A remains pending the EasyCanvas hardware Gate and is not PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Long Stroke Live upstream / pointerup profiling keeps Raw Gesture authoritative and separates it from a bounded incremental live working path. New Raw points feed at most 192 live working samples plus a pen-tip tail; incremental Raw overlay and pressure statistics avoid full-Raw pointermove scans, Live preview Material is capped at 256 presentation samples, and the existing 192-segment Cylinder Proxy remains the live priority. Final adaptive Material Samples remain uncapped for fidelity. The latest 6970-point / 32.285-second fixture is recorded as 972 controls (957 initial + 15 refinement), 7769 Smooth samples, 7211 Material samples, effective resolution 131, 123288 triangles, and one component. A spatial KD-tree reduces the full 559688976 voxel×sample candidate budget to 2521108 measured local candidates with the same SDF within 1e-6 on fixture comparisons. Control fitting tolerance is now independent of material Thickness. Host profiling and automated tests pass; EasyCanvas long-duration fps / pointerup→READY / console Gate remains pending, so HANA-2A is not PASS / FROZEN and no commit/push was made.

HANA-2A Mouse Edit latency refinement separates authoritative edits from visual input handling. Pointermove keeps only the latest client position and event timestamp; a pending requestAnimationFrame applies that latest position to the adaptive Control Stroke, derives a deterministic maximum-128-control / maximum-256-sample preview, and reuses the existing maximum-192-segment Cylinder Proxy. Intermediate pointer positions are not displayed, while pointerup flushes the latest position before the authoritative Smooth → Material → Field → Surface rebuild. Nearest Centerline picking reuses the cached authoritative Centerline, and Raw overlay rendering uses a cached Path2D. Debug timing records event/handler/latest-state/rAF/preview/render timestamps, queue age, pointer and preview rates, coalesced moves, pending rAF, oldest pointer age, and Long Tasks. Surface / Centerline / Samples are whole-button touch toggles with 48px hit areas and ON / OFF state labels; defaults remain Surface ON, Centerline ON, Samples OFF. Hardware Gate remains pending; no PASS / FROZEN or commit / push.

HANA-2A Mouse Edit session lifecycle diagnosis adds HANA-local resource telemetry for consecutive Edit sessions. Surface replacement disposes the previous Mesh, BufferGeometry, and Material; the bounded 192-instance Proxy is reused; Edit sessions add no pointer listeners or spatial index. Browser smoke across 11 consecutive sessions kept scene objects at 6, Surface Mesh at 1, Proxy object at 1, BufferGeometry at 5, Material at 5, GPU geometries at 5, and GPU textures at 0, without monotonic E2E or resource growth. Session history records pointer / preview counts, queue / E2E / render stats, and before/after resources. The host did not reproduce accumulation; if hardware still slows after the first Final rebuild, GPU command queue / presentation remains a FOLLOW-UP. HANA-2A remains pending hardware verification and is not PASS / FROZEN; no commit / push.

HANA-2A A/B diagnosis compared immediate versus 5-second-delayed Edit #2 and Surface ON versus OFF on the same authoritative geometry. Host/browser Edit preview latency stayed similar; Surface OFF removed render triangles but did not reveal a large CPU edit difference. Resource counts and geometry counts showed no session-only monotonic growth, and the picker uses projection-based nearest queries rather than Surface Mesh raycast. The confirmed HANA-side issue was long-stroke Right-view hit testing of non-visible controls, which caused a view-plane-miss and stopped preview updates after a prior edit; nearest candidates now require projected visibility. EasyCanvas end-to-end latency and GPU presentation remain pending hardware verification; HANA-2A is not PASS / FROZEN and no commit / push.

HANA-2A presentation A/B diagnosis records Edit-time render targets. The default hide-final path hides the previous Final Surface on pointerdown and shows only the bounded Edit Preview Proxy; the diagnostic final-visible URL keeps both visible. Browser inspection confirmed hide-final as final draw 0 / preview draw 4 and final-visible as final draw 4 / preview draw 4, with pointerup restoring Final Surface visible and Preview hidden. Host Edit #2 did not show a large latency difference between the paths; EasyCanvas end-to-end visual latency and GPU presentation remain pending. Raw Gesture, adaptive Control, tolerance 0.09, dense Final Material, Shape Fidelity, provenance, pressure/time/order, and the 192-segment Proxy cap remain unchanged. HANA-2A is not PASS / FROZEN; no commit / push.

HANA-2A visual alignment diagnosis adds optional HANA-local DOM markers behind ?editMarkers=1. During Mouse Edit, red P shows the latest pointer event position, blue T shows the projected edit target Control Point, and green X shows the projected Live Proxy tip; all are latest-pointer-wins and updated without WebGL or geometry calculation in the same requestAnimationFrame path. Per-session event / marker / WebGL frame counts, coordinates, and final rAF timestamps are written to debug dataset and session history. Normal B presentation remains Final Surface hidden / Edit Preview visible during Edit, then Final visible / Preview hidden on pointerup. PC Mouse and EasyCanvas use the same diagnostic URLs. Raw Gesture, adaptive Control, tolerance 0.09, Final Material density, Shape Fidelity, provenance, pressure/time/order, Live Proxy 192 cap, and SKIN remain unchanged; hardware Case A/B/C/D classification is pending, so HANA-2A is not PASS / FROZEN and no commit / push.

HANA-2A T-to-X pipeline diagnosis adds per-rAF stage timing from Edit Target through preview Control / Smooth / Material, Proxy segment generation, instance matrix update, DOM Proxy tip, and render submission. The diagnostic default remains bounded preview; ?editMarkers=1&editProxy=direct bypasses preview geometry and sends one diagnostic segment directly from the authoritative Edit Target to the reused Proxy. Direct mode is diagnosis-only and does not change Raw Gesture, adaptive Control, Soft Edit, Final density, Shape Fidelity, provenance, or the 192-segment cap. Hardware Edit #1 / #2 / #3 / #10 comparison is still pending; HANA-2A remains FAIL / not PASS / FROZEN and no commit / push.

HANA startup recovery prevents a missing WebGL2 context from aborting HANA before viewport chrome and pointer listeners initialize. A HANA-local no-op renderer fallback keeps 2D Raw Gesture, Pencil Draw, camera math, and diagnostics available; 3D Surface still requires a WebGL-capable browser. Pencil input now enters Draw on Front / Right / Top when no authoritative Stroke exists, while Mouse Edit / Camera behavior is unchanged. WebGL-capable browser smoke reached Raw 9, Control 2, Smooth 9, Material 48, and Surface READY with 3600 triangles. HANA-2A remains pending hardware Gate and is not PASS / FROZEN; no commit / push.

Repeated hardware Surface Mouse Edit observation: Edit #1 is fast; after pointerup, Edit #2 catches briefly at the start and then remains markedly slow. Existing resource/session telemetry did not reproduce accumulation, and the cause remains unconfirmed. Combined with fast P / Edit Target and slow X / Proxy observations, the next comparison remains T → bounded preview → Proxy → render presentation on real hardware. HANA-2A stays FAIL / hardware recheck pending; Raw Gesture, adaptive Control, Final Material, Shape Fidelity, provenance, pressure/time/order, Live Proxy 192 cap, SKIN, and next Phase remain unchanged.

HANA-2A T-to-X diagnosis adds per-session pointer revisions and a 120-frame ring-buffer trace for Target, bounded Control, Smooth, Material, Proxy, and Render, with same-rAF validation. The existing bounded path remains the default; editMarkers=1&editProxy=direct remains a diagnosis-only one-segment Target → Proxy A/B path. Browser smoke confirmed matching revisions within each consumed rAF for both paths; hardware latency classification remains pending. Raw Gesture, adaptive Control, Soft Edit, Final density, Shape Fidelity, provenance, pressure/time/order, Live Proxy 192 cap, SKIN, and next Phase remain unchanged; HANA-2A is not PASS / FROZEN.

HANA-2A Final Surface finalization diagnosis adds explicit generation identity and state transitions from pointerup through CPU-ready, renderer upload submission, first render, next-rAF presentation, and READY. Per-generation stage timestamps, geometry / Field workload counts, renderer BufferGeometry / attribute bytes, heap samples when available, and request/start/CPU/upload/apply/stale counts are exposed in HANA-local debug data. finalProfile=normal, skip, cpu-only, and upload-only provide deterministic CPU / upload / presentation A/B paths; no fidelity, adaptive Control, Material density, Proxy 192 cap, or SKIN changes were made. Browser smoke passed all four profile paths with console warning/error 0; EasyCanvas Edit #1–#10 and pointerup→READY hardware recheck remain pending, so HANA-2A is not PASS / FROZEN and no commit / push.

HANA-2A Final Surface pointerup refinement keeps the authoritative Field / SDF / mesh semantics and dense adaptive Material fidelity unchanged, but extracts the final mesh cooperatively in contiguous Z slices with browser yields between slices. During normal finalization the previous Final Surface is hidden while the live Preview Proxy remains visible; after the new mesh is uploaded, the next requestAnimationFrame presents Final and removes the Proxy. Browser smoke recorded a 6.7ms pointerup handler and 476.5ms pointerup→READY for a short stroke, and the cooperative mesh matched the synchronous mesh exactly in tests. EasyCanvas hardware recheck is still required; HANA-2A remains FAIL / not PASS / FROZEN and no commit / push.

HANA-2A repeated-Edit refinement cancels a pending older Final generation when a new Mouse Edit starts. Cooperative extraction stops at the next Z slice boundary, stale mesh results are not uploaded or presented, and only the newest Final request proceeds. Final resolution, adaptive Material density, Raw / Control / Smooth fidelity, provenance, pressure/time/order, and Live Proxy 192 cap are unchanged. HANA tests 33, TypeScript, Vite build, and browser console warning/error 0 passed; EasyCanvas repeated-Edit recheck remains pending, so HANA-2A stays FAIL / not PASS / FROZEN with no commit / push.

HANA-2A final real-device Gate passed on iPad Pro 11-inch with Apple Pencil through EasyCanvas into Windows Browser. Long Surface strokes supported repeated Mouse Edit without accumulating latency; Live Proxy remained smooth; pointerup returned to READY without a long whole-screen stop; finalization could be superseded by a new Edit; stale Final generations did not interrupt newer results; Surface / Centerline / Samples touch toggles, normal and diagnostic URLs, Shape Fidelity, Right View axis constraints, component validity, and continuous Surface presentation all passed. HANA-2A is now PASS / FROZEN. Frozen hierarchy is Raw Gesture → adaptive geometry-error-bounded Control Stroke (tolerance 0.09, Thickness-independent) → Smooth Centerline → dense adaptive Material Samples → KD-tree Point Field / SDF → derived Surface Mesh. Raw metadata, Final density, Live Proxy 192 cap, and JSON authoritative boundaries remain unchanged. Known limitations are documented: very dense long Final generation takes time but remains cooperative, minor late long-stroke live follow-up may remain, Soft Edit is control-count based pending arc-length follow-up, environment-specific uv_os_get_passwd ENOMEM is not an implementation failure, and Chrome command-line warnings are not HANA console errors. HANA tests 33/33, TypeScript, full Vite build, browser smoke, manifest validation, diff check, and console warning/error 0 passed; src/studies/skin diff is 0. No next Phase, Flower, Worker, WebGPU, CUDA, or SKIN Bridge work is included.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 4 adds npm run dev:hana:lan. The Windows launcher starts the loopback-only CPU Compute Service on 5483 and the HANA LAN Vite server on 5482, prints a private IPv4 HANA URL, proxies /api/hana-compute through same-origin Vite, and stops both children on Ctrl+C. HANA_LAN_PORT, HANA_COMPUTE_PORT, and HANA_COMPUTE_WORKERS are configurable. Normal local Vite remains on 5174; Firewall, Wi-Fi, and iPad Remote Finalization verification remain pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 5 adds HANA-local LOCAL / WINDOWS / AUTO compute controls. Windows mode sends only the current Stroke's versioned Finalization Snapshot to the same-origin compute endpoint after pointerup, receives validated binary typed arrays, preserves bounded Live Preview, cancels stale generations, and restores the final Surface only for the newest result. AUTO uses the documented work estimate and falls back to Local unless strict mode is requested. Browser smoke through the LAN Vite proxy passed with console warning/error 0; iPad Pro / Apple Pencil / EasyCanvas Remote Gate remains pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 6 fixes protocol and parity coverage. Binary Finalization results use a bounded aligned header + raw Float32 / Uint32 payload without base64; truncation, size limits, array descriptors, and deterministic Local/Core wire round-trip are tested. Node Windows backend integration matches the service result. CPU engine hana-cpu-js-v0 remains the only implementation and iPad Remote Gate remains pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 7 adds HANA-local object-level finalization. HanaRemoteObjectCoordinator schedules independent authoring objects by active / visible / background priority with bounded concurrency, same-object cancellation, latest-generation checks, stale result rejection, and result/error callbacks. Authoring Document Stroke jobs preserve Raw Gesture ID, Control provenance, curve, material mapping intent, and object revisions without saving derived geometry. Flower / cluster and iPad Remote Gate remain pending; no global union or SKIN production connection was added.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 8 documents and benchmarks AUTO policy. Short / medium / long deterministic fixtures expose controls, smooth, adaptive Material Samples, estimated voxels, and the documented Local versus Windows recommendation; optional --compute measures CPU Finalization without reducing fidelity. AUTO still requires a ready Remote health check and falls back to Local unless computeStrict=1. GPU remains false and iPad / EasyCanvas verification is pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 9 isolates the Windows worker behind the explicit HanaComputeEngine interface. CpuJsHanaComputeEngine is the only v0 implementation (hana-cpu-js-v0); its fixed capabilities are binaryMesh=true, cancellation=true, objectLevelFinalization=true, and gpu=false. Engine results match the shared Finalization Core, while GPU / WebGPU / CUDA implementation remains out of scope. Software milestones pass; iPad Pro / Apple Pencil / EasyCanvas Remote Gate remains pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 10 completes object-level Finalization on top of existing Authoring Document identity and revision. Dirty dependency resolution separates direct, dependent, and independent clean objects; same-object jobs carry documentRevision, objectRevision, snapshot generation as objectGenerationId, and algorithmVersion; coordinator cancellation is same-object only, priority is active/visible/background, and result application requires all identity fields to match. Presentation-only object results never become Authoring Document or Mesh authority. Software tests pass; multi-object iPad Remote Gate remains pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 11 centralizes deterministic AUTO policy in hanaComputePolicy.ts. Lightweight estimates include Smooth, adaptive Material Samples, bounds volume, estimated voxels, candidate estimate, object count, and dependency count; thresholds remain 512 Material Samples or 200,000 voxels. AUTO chooses Local for light or unhealthy Remote, Windows for heavy healthy work, caches recent health, reports selection reasons, and falls back to Local only for the current generation after a Remote failure. The benchmark covers short, medium, long, Flower, Small Cluster, Multiple Objects, and Surface Draw estimates, with optional short/medium CPU measurement; iPad / Apple Pencil / EasyCanvas AUTO Gate remains pending.

Remote Compute v0 Milestone 12 formalizes the versioned hana-compute-capability.v0 CPU-only engine boundary: engineId, algorithmVersion, executionKind, gpu, cancellation/object-level support, and supported snapshot/protocol versions. Only CpuJsHanaComputeEngine (cpu-js-v0) is registered; unknown engine IDs are rejected explicitly, and compatibility is checked before computation and when applying results. No CUDA, WebGPU, DirectCompute, Vulkan, or GPU server is implemented. Software Gate passes; iPad Remote Gate remains pending.

HANA Authoring Stack v0 interaction layer adds a compact touch-first control pane for iPad Pro 11-inch, bounded live-path profiling, latest-frame Pencil preview processing, lifecycle and WebGL context diagnostics, versioned IndexedDB local recovery checkpoints, touch pan/pinch navigation, view presets, Fit View, and stoppable Auto Rotate. Raw Gesture fidelity, adaptive Control tolerance 0.09, dense Final Material / Field / Surface semantics, Remote Compute v0, and Live Proxy 192 cap remain unchanged. Software verification is required before the iPad hardware recheck; HANA-local only, with no SKIN production changes.

Raw Gesture Capture Integrity v0 separates authoritative Pointer / coalesced sample capture from the bounded latest-frame preview scheduler. The capture boundary keeps every coalesced sample, adds the parent PointerEvent when it is not already represented by the final coalesced sample, and suppresses only exact duplicate samples by pointerId, x, y, pressure, and timestamp. Pointerup / cancel samples use the same boundary. HANA-local diagnostics report Raw count, unique count, remaining and suppressed exact duplicates, interval median / p95 / max, >50ms and >100ms gaps, largest spatial jump, monotonic time, and parent/coalesced source counts. No interpolation, proximity decimation, Raw mutation, Control / Material fidelity reduction, Remote Compute redesign, or SKIN change was introduced.

HANA Long-Stroke Main-Thread Starvation Diagnosis / Fix v0 adds development-only RAW ONLY, RAW + CONTROL, RAW + CONTROL + SMOOTH, RAW + CONTROL + SMOOTH + LIVE PROXY, and FULL CURRENT LIVE PATH + RENDER isolation modes. Raw capture remains synchronous and authoritative; live diagnostics refresh at most 250ms and no longer run on every PointerEvent. FULL provisional Surface preview uses cooperative Z-slice meshing with single-flight and generation invalidation, while Final Surface remains an existing pointerup operation. Per-stage timing, 50/100/200/400/800/1600/3200/5000/10000 checkpoints, event-loop lag, live-stroke-only long-task counts, and gap correlation are exposed locally. HANA-2A, Remote Compute, SKIN production, geometry fidelity, and the 192-segment Live Proxy cap remain unchanged; iPad 5/10/20-second hardware recheck remains pending.
